name: Jeddah
short_description: A coastal city blending coral architecture with modern waterfronts.
full_description: Jeddah, historically the gateway for pilgrims and traders, combines heritage architecture with modern coastal areas. It offers stunning beaches, historical districts like Al-Balad, and a rich culinary scene.

shopping.name: Red Sea Mall
shopping.experience_summary: One of the biggest and most popular malls in Jeddah with a massive variety of brands.
shopping.signature_dish: Chicken Tikka Masala and Garlic Naan
shopping.local_tip: Brew 92 is a legendary local coffee roastery; don't leave without trying their flat white.

shopping.name: Jeddah Park
shopping.experience_summary: A new architectural masterpiece offering a mix of shopping and luxury interior design.
shopping.top_activity: Visit the stunning indoor fountain and art installations
shopping.local_tip: The mall is very spacious, perfect for a long walk away from the humidity.

shopping.name: Jeddah Boulevard
shopping.experience_summary: An open-air luxury destination for high-end fashion and elite dining.
shopping.local_tip: Baco offers a unique Asian-Latin fusion; try their tacos for a quick bite.

nature_and_beach.name: White Island
nature_and_beach.experience_summary: A hidden gem for boat trips and crystal clear waters.
nature_and_beach.top_activity: Snorkeling and swimming in turquoise water
nature_and_beach.local_tip: Book a private boat from Obhur early in the morning for the best experience.

nature_and_beach.name: Corniche Park
nature_and_beach.experience_summary: The newly developed waterfront with running tracks and sea views.
nature_and_beach.local_tip: Rent a bike and ride towards the new sculptures area.

nature_and_beach.name: Al-Abhur Creek
nature_and_beach.experience_summary: The heart of Jeddah's water sports and private beach resorts.
nature_and_beach.top_activity: Jet skiing or a sunset boat cruise
nature_and_beach.local_tip: Twina is the best place to experience authentic Jeddawi fried fish.

heritage_and_landmarks.name: Historic Al-Balad
heritage_and_landmarks.experience_summary: A UNESCO World Heritage site with ancient coral-stone houses.
heritage_and_landmarks.top_activity: Walking through the narrow alleys and Roshan balconies
heritage_and_landmarks.local_tip: Try the 'Sobia' drink during your walk; it's a traditional Jeddawi favorite.

heritage_and_landmarks.name: King Fahd Fountain
heritage_and_landmarks.experience_summary: The tallest fountain of its kind in the world, an iconic symbol of Jeddah.
heritage_and_landmarks.top_activity: Watching the fountain lighting show at night
heritage_and_landmarks.local_tip: The best view is from the Ritz-Carlton or the nearby public seating area at night.

heritage_and_landmarks.name: Islamic Arts Center
heritage_and_landmarks.experience_summary: A cultural hub showcasing the beauty and history of Islamic calligraphy and arts.
heritage_and_landmarks.top_activity: Explore the rare collection of manuscripts
heritage_and_landmarks.local_tip: Check for workshops if you're interested in learning calligraphy.

heritage_and_landmarks.name: Jeddah Art Walk
heritage_and_landmarks.experience_summary: A modern outdoor art gallery by the sea featuring food trucks and lights.
heritage_and_landmarks.top_activity: Photoshoot with the neon art installations
heritage_and_landmarks.local_tip: Section-B is widely considered the best burger spot in the city; expect a queue!

travel_tips: Explore Al-Balad for its unique coral-stone architecture and ancient vibes.
The humidity can be high; always carry water and wear light fabrics.
King Fahd Fountain is best viewed from the Corniche after 7 PM.
Use 'Barn's' for a quick, reliable local coffee fix while driving.
